  - Noticed urine pink today; no frank red blood reported other than today.
  - No fever, nausea, or vomiting.
- Time line
  - Symptoms described as starting about 3 days ago at first, later clarified as just under a week; inconsistency in onset noted.
  - Symptoms currently persistent.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors
  - Pain related to urination; no clear relief factors described.
- Associated symptoms
  - No back pain, no systemic symptoms (fever, chills).
  - Bowel habits usually IBS-related; no new bowel symptoms.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection / cystitis suspected.
  - Plan:
    - Start empiric antibiotics for 3 days (trimethoprim or nitrofurantoin); exact dose, route, and frequency not documented.

    - For pain, consider paracetamol as needed.
    - If symptoms do not improve by next week, re-evaluate with follow-up.
    - Monitor for red-flag symptoms: fever, back pain, vomiting; if these occur, contact the clinic.

- General follow-up
  - If urine culture/analysis returns positive, antibiotics will be guided by results.
  - Return visit planned if persistent symptoms.
